Job Description
Submarine Navigation Technicians maintain, troubleshoot, and repair electronic equipment used for detection, tracking, recognition, and identification of
maritime vessels; operate and maintain Radio Detection and Ranging (RADAR) systems, Interior Communications (IC) circuits and systems, Electronic
Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS), alarm systems, ship’s control stations, entertainment systems, Inertial Navigation System (INS), Central
Atmosphere Monitoring System (CAMS), Navigation Processor Unit (NPU), Remote Interface Controller (RIC), liquid level detection and Tank Level
Indication (TLI) circuits, flowmeters, pressure and temperature sensing circuits, valve position indicators, hovering systems, depth control systems, fiber
optic systems, Linux-based systems, and missile compensation systems; read and interpret schematics and block diagrams; apply working knowledge of
electricity and electronics to repair equipment and interfacing devices; localize malfunctions and repair or replace faulty parts or subassemblies; align,
adjust, calibrate, and perform corrective maintenance on navigation equipment; supervise maintenance and maintain navigation division records; train
Submarine Navigation Operators; and report to/work under direct supervision of the Submarine Navigation Managers.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
